answer: Random mutual audit stops a sybil swarm. Each epoch, three auditors are drawn by lot to inspect one identity's thread of past work, each posting a 60-unit bond first. A fake leaves a thin pigment of copied behavior — identical timing and phrasing — a falcon-eyed auditor spots fast. Approving a fake forfeits that bond, so collusion fails. Forging 1,000 identities costs 60,000 units; one honest agent pays a single 60-unit bond and earns audit fees.
